snippet.text: | `melian dismiss <range\|#pr> <id> --reason <text> [--only] [--records dir:<path>]` | Dismisses a finding of the stored review, recording the reason, the git author, and the time, and decides the verdict again, so `findings` and `publish` count the finding out. Dismissing a dismissed finding replaces its reason and keeps the old one in its history. A finding's own ID dismisses it with the reports adjudication merged into it by snippet, and the output names each by rule, check, and ID; a report merged only through a hunk stays live. The ID of a merged report dismisses that report alone, and `--only` dismisses the report the speaker's ID names alone. The output lists every report it left live under "Still live, merged with it before:" Reads only local refs and storage, as `findings` does. `--records dir:<path>` writes each dismissal's record to a directory store at once, superseding the dismissals of the finding that stand there, by [the decision that a dismissal record is written once](../decisions/2026-11-18-a-dismissal-record-is-written-once.md). It refuses, before recording anything, unless the base commit's root `melian.yaml` writes `trust.writers: true` out, as `review --records` does, and names on stderr each dismissal it left unshared. It is all or nothing: a store it cannot list, or that fails the write, makes it refuse, name the store, and record nothing, on the host or in the store. Without `--records` it says the dismissal is not shared, and that dismissing it again with `--records` shares it: no review exports a dismissal made with no store, and each review names it as unshared, by [the decision that a shared dismissal holds only at its own revision](../decisions/2026-11-20-a-shared-dismissal-holds-only-at-its-own-revision.md) | `0` recorded, `1` when nothing is stored or the verdict has no finding with the ID, when `--records` names a store the base does not trust or that fails, or when the dismissal was recorded but the verdict could not be decided again, which the message says, `64`  [cut at 2 KiB]

snippet.text: - `SharedRecord.parse` checks rules 2 to 4: the fields and no other, the patterns of `changeset`, `kind` and `revision`, a sorted `supersedes` only on a dismissal, post, status, `ledger-comment` or comparison, and `signer` with `signature`. A dismissal carries no revision, by rule 5. `SharedRecord.parse` takes payload checks keyed by kind, and refuses a record whose kind has none with `unvalidatedKind`, so a kind is never taken on trust before the build that defines its payload registers its check. Core checks one payload itself: a round's manifest, by rule 4. It holds `read`, the kind, key and ID of every record the round read, sorted by ID; `walkthrough`, its key and ID or `null`; `replaces`, the earlier rounds of its revision it replaces; and `before`, the rounds it follows: those of the revision before, or the store's frontier from a host with no history of the changeset. It holds nothing else. `testPayloads` in `@melian-agent/core/testing` takes any payload of every other kind, for tests alone.

snippet.text: Six gaps err towards blocking. The records hold no history, so without `seenBefore` every finding reads new. A finding the host holds dismissed by inheritance reads live here, until [issue #506](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/506). A dismissal stored before findings document version 11 holds no frozen sighting, gets no record, and reads live. A record an older build of this step wrote holds no lens status and no account, and reads not reviewed. An account [pull request #476](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/476) wrote, at version 1, reads not reviewed too; `test/fixtures/account-v1/` holds one main wrote at `4d08b08c`. A dismissal of a static finding gets a record only when a stored request proves that the run its sighting was stamped with asked for check code storing none of its tool's text. Without one the export leaves it out, the review names it in `unshared` with the code `unprovenRun`, `melian review` prints it as a warning, and the reader sees the finding undismissed. One difference does not: a dismissal record is never withdrawn, so a dismissal withdrawn by hand would still read dismissed here; no command withdraws one today, and a host's reopen reaches the reader because a dismissal holds only at the revision it was made at, and there only while each round since meets its trigger, as [the decision that a shared dismissal holds only at its own revision](../decisions/2026-11-20-a-shared-dismissal-holds-only-at-its-own-revision.md) says.

snippet.text: `findings.test.ts` reads a dismissal of an introduced finding sighted later as affected with a new trigger: the host and the reader both reopen it. It also drives the host through the three revisions and reads the third with the hunks of the sightings shared: the host and the reader both read `new`, and without the second revision's sighting the reader reads `dismissed`. `recorded-round.test.ts` pins the rule through records and rounds, and remembers no hunk the round it reads cites. A lens record, and a check record, that a round after the dismissal names and that cite a hunk the revision no longer holds reopen it. A record no round names reopens nothing. A dismissal made again after that round, or at the revision read, holds. A chain that names a round the set lacks, a round whose record the set lacks, or a round of another changeset leaves the finding live, and so does a chain, or one branch of a fork, that ends before the dismissal's revision; a fork where either branch cites a changed hunk reopens it, and one where neither does keeps it. `review-records-export.test.ts` has three hosts review three revisions, the second and third with no history of the changeset: each round names the one before it, and the dismissal the first host made still reaches the third round's reader. With a forked store, a fresh host's round names both branches, and when host A reviews again after host B, A's round names both its own earlier round and B's.

snippet.text: The reader decides a round only at the revision its round record names: a caller's revision with another base or head reads as not reviewed, since a dismissal tested against another revision's hunks proves nothing. For a caller that decides each sighting itself, `contents(revision)` hands over at that revision what the verdict is decided from: the revision's key, every sighting the round's records hold, the revision's proving hunks, and each dismissal record of the changeset that counts, with its record ID, the finding it dismisses and the revision its sighting was seen at. At another revision, or for a round its records cannot stand for, it returns the reason instead. The reader applies a dismissal record by [the dismissal record decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-a-dismissal-record-holds-what-melian-dismiss-stored.md). It reads every dismissal record of the changeset that counts, the latest by time for each finding, the greater ID on a tie, and passes them to `mergeSightings` with the revision's proving hunks. A dismissal holds only for a round at the revision it was made at, by [the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-20](../decisions/2026-11-20-a-shared-dismissal-holds-only-at-its-own-revision.md). The rounds since it are every round of the changeset in the set that the record's `frontier` does not name, the round read among them. If any of them reviewed another revision, the dismissal has ended, and `contents` hands it over in `ended` with that round and its revision. Otherwise a finding reads dismissed when every sighting of it in those rounds meets the record's trigger under `reopens` and cites only hunks the revision holds, as `sharedDismissalHolds` applies it. The finding stays live when the record does not count, names no frontier, or a sighting fails that test, and when a round since names a record the set does not hold, or names in `before` a round that neither the set nor the frontier holds, the one thing `before` still decides. For a caller that decides each sighting itself, `contents(revision)` hands over at that revision what the verdict is decided from: the revision's key, every sighting the round's records hold, the revision's proving hunks, and each dismissal record of the changeset that counts, with its record ID, the finding it dismisses and the revision its sighting was seen at. At another revision, or for a round its records cannot stand for, it returns the reason instead. The reader applies a dismissal record by [the dismissal record decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-a-dismissal-record-holds-what-melian-dismiss-stored.md). It reads every dismissal record of the changeset that counts, the latest by time for each finding, the greater ID on a tie, and passes them to `mergeSightings` with the revision's proving hunks. A dismissal holds only for a round at the revision it was made at, by [the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-20](../decisions/2026-11-20-a-shared-dismissal-holds-only-at-its-own-revision.md). The rounds since it are every round of the changeset in the set that the record's `frontier` does not name, the round read among them. If any of them reviewed another revision, the dismissal has ended, and `contents` hands it over in `ended` with that round and its revision. Otherwise a finding reads dismissed when every sighting of it in those rounds meets the record's trigger under `reopens` and cites only hunks the revision holds, as `sharedDismissalHolds` applies it. The finding stays live when the record does not count, names no frontier, or a sighting fails that test, and when a round since names a record the set does not hold, or names in `before` a round that neither the set nor the frontier holds, the one thing `before` still decides. The reader reads no git and no other revision's hunks, so it is never looser than any host, and a push leaves the finding live until someone dismisses it again. A round names in `before` the rounds of its host's previous revision, joined with every round of another revision in the review's store listing that no other such round names, as [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-18-a-shared-reader-remembers-every-cited-hunk.md) says. `verificationRan` is set only when the account names the verifier, since a host round with every finding dismissed runs none and exports no claim of an earlier verification. A dismissed finding therefore carries no verification in the reader's verdict, where the host's shows an earlier round's; [issue #506](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/506) closes that.

Problem: a review that waited for every wave of the lens task waited for another review's, whose verifier could be waiting on it in turn. Example: [main's restatement test](../../packages/pipeline/test/restatement.test.ts) holds review A's first verifier request until review B, with another verifier route, finishes; B waited for A's wave and neither finished. When another review's final task has retired this review's own wave outcome for a candidate it still holds, the final commit refuses, unless the review attaches to that task, and the review records the verifier `failed` with `superseded` and leaves the restatement links alone, as a review whose final task another replaced does. The next review asks the verifier again about such a root, by [the decision that a review reads its dismissals once](../decisions/2026-11-18-a-review-reads-its-dismissals-once.md). Problem: the first form of this rule kept the shown dismissals only for the waves the same call started, in memory. Example: a review crashed after its wave judged the root and before its final step; the maintainer replaced the root's dismissal; the retry reused the wave and inherited the replacement. A review that attaches to an existing final task re-derives its links under the dismissals it reads, as every round does. `startVerification` keeps the final key's shape, so a repeat review attaches as before. It unlocks and clears only what it will ask for. The commit that creates a new final task also drops every wave candidate whose claims it clears, so a wave a later verification replaced never stands again: a review under verifier route A, then B, then A once more asks A again rather than reuse its old wave over B's stored verdict. The same commit drops any wave that has not finished, so a wave another review's watcher started just before it can spawn and report nothing. Once the index names a final verification, `startWave` refuses, so a watcher still running in another review cannot clear what the final task decided. The same commit refuses an input whose reused outcome no wave stands for any longer, when another review's final task retired that wave, and the review records the verifier `failed` with `superseded`: the wave's verdicts are gone, so copying its `done` would let a claim nobody judged pass, and the candidate's credentials were unlocked for the outcome it reused, not for a new request. [Issue #313](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/313) holds the redesign that would fence every such race in one commit. The task copies a reused outcome into its result and spawns no conversation for it. Under `rerun`, a wave outcome that was not done, or that finished on a refused model, is asked again. A task is owned when the index names it as its revision's verification, or when the wave document names it under the lens task the index names and no later wave verified any of its claims; `VerificationWaves.owns` answers both, for the spawn, failover and report commits and for the sweep. A triage replacement that detaches verification deletes the revision's waves too, so the sweep aborts any still live. Stage telemetry reads the waves' verifier conversations beside the final task's. `test/verification-waves.test.ts` holds a slow lens open, and `test/review-crash.test.ts` kills a review once a wave's report has committed and before the slower lens ends.

snippet.text: A reader that cannot resolve such a revision refuses the round, as not reviewed, and names why: a commit the checkout lacks, by its hash, as a shallow clone may, or a read with no checkout at all. It never lets the dismissal hold. The refusal says how to recover: fetch the history, or dismiss the finding again with `--records`.
